summary: This sermon addresses doubt and faith through the story of Thomas encountering the risen Jesus. The pastor argues that doubt is natural and can be answered through apologetics—rational evidence for Christianity from science, archaeology, and history—but emphasizes that the ultimate goal is not just intellectual certainty but experiencing 'Zoe,' the abundant, unshakable life found only in relationship with Jesus.
key_points: Jesus responds to Thomas's doubt with peace and proof, not condemnation
Apologetics (defense of faith) helps remove barriers to trusting God
Science, archaeology, and historical records corroborate Biblical accounts
Physical and emotional needs ('bios' and 'psyche') can never be fully satisfied
True abundant life ('Zoe') comes only through Jesus and brings lasting peace
big_idea: While evidence and apologetics can remove intellectual barriers to faith, true abundant life is found not in satisfying physical or emotional needs but in the unshakable peace that comes from trusting Jesus as the source of eternal life.
title: Resurrection Rumors: Doubting Thomas
